dispositions.rationale: Text unchanged since the merged record's round, where this lens read it without objection; on substance: every sentence of BRF-A9 is decided by the one grammar-fixture test family, and the counterpart markings are how each suite's fixture test finds the parser it checks; one observation, one obligation.

Text unchanged since the merged record's round, where this lens read it without objection; on substance: the third-section clause was placed on BRF-A22 by the merged round's accepted obligation-reduction-6, and both clauses are observed by the one section comparison the suite makes over the same three outputs.

Text unchanged since the merged record's round, where this lens read it without objection; on substance: one observation, two runs in one directory with outputs and directory compared, decides all three clauses of BRF-A30; no write and nothing shared are what make the repeated result identical.
Repeats obligation-reduction-5 of the merged record: the installer stages the skill directory whole, and the evaluation runs the skill from source by full path (BRF-D8).

Repeats obligation-reduction-1 of the merged record: the per-brief guard is check (BRF-A8, BRF-A23), which BRF-A28 makes the skill require before every dispatch; the evaluation claims fidelity over its fixtures under the stochastic rule.
Repeats obligation-reduction-2 of the merged record: evidence fidelity in any brief is what check --checks decides (BRF-A23).
Repeats obligation-reduction-3 of the merged record: the writer sees one refusal shape whatever the code; F3 to F5 sample the refusal sources, and BRF-A28 reads the relay instruction in the skill.

F6 samples the writer's judgment on one infeasible check, and judging feasibility in code is out of scope by the spec's own list; BRF-D8 states that five runs measure the scope sentence and never prove it.

Text unchanged since the merged record's round, where this lens read it without objection; on substance: BRF-A24 observes the behaviour the constraint protects, that the helper runs where nothing third-party is importable; an optional import that changes nothing observable is a code-review read, as the merged record's obligation-reduction-10 rules for a second resolver.

Text unchanged since the merged record's round, where this lens read it without objection; on substance: BRF-A28 judges the skill text as S3.4's deliverable and F1 to F7 judge the writer's behaviour under BRF-A16 to BRF-A20; neither claims the other (merged record, behavioural-outcome-1).
The installer prunes every test file and every evals/ directory by its own .installignore, and that staging check is the installer's gate, outside this spec's scope.
Repeats obligation-reduction-11 of the merged record: content-lint measures every deployed skill body against its cap and fails the gate above it.
Repeats obligation-reduction-12 of the merged record: the attestation is the record; the tree cannot observe the execution it attests (BRF-D8).

The fingerprint excludes evals/, so a scorer change alters no fingerprint and BRF-A33 keeps every lock current or fallen on its stored runs; whether the operator dispatches writers anyway is an act the tree cannot observe.
Repeats obligation-reduction-13 of the merged record: BRF-D8 states the repeat limit is an operator procedure because no output shows a retry.

Rests on the operator, as the merged record's obligation-reduction-14 states: nothing in the committed tree can observe a run, output or report that was never committed, nor one replaced before commit.

Rests on the operator, as the merged record's obligation-reduction-14 states: nothing in the committed tree can observe a run, output or report that was never committed, nor one replaced before commit. The record names the outputs that count and BRF-A35 refuses a sixth.

Reading a failed run and judging it a defect is the operator's act. BRF-D8 states the response, changing the skill, which voids the lock, as procedure, and the scope excludes judging in code what only a reading decides.
The verification child's ownership is what the tracker observes, not the tree; BRF-D9 states it, and the parent's closing rule belongs to the parent spec's ACQ-D2, outside this document's criteria.

Text unchanged since the merged record's round, where this lens read it without objection; on substance: rule 4 says a heading ends an entry, and that heading is then a nonblank line outside an entry, which BRF-A7 refuses by line; the two rules give one outcome, refusal, and a criteria file is the bare list BRF-D2 describes.

Text unchanged since the merged record's round, where this lens read it without objection; on substance: the checks file is read by the stdlib JSON parser, whose last-key-wins reading emit inherits, and BRF-A6 covers the duplicate-ID case at the sources the writer assigns; a repeated key inside the writer's own checks file is a limit JSON itself declines to represent, and BRF-A23's check --checks surfaces the kept entry when it is the incomplete one.

Text unchanged since the merged record's round, where this lens read it without objection; on substance: BRF-D2 lists --ids as a parameter of the --spec source, not a source flag, so --item or --criteria with --ids is a flag outside that source's grammar; S3.1's argument parsing refuses it as source-conflict naming the flags given, which BRF-A29 observes by that phrase.

parts.statement: The delivered artifacts occupy those specified locations, including the helper beside SKILL.md.

obligations.source: BRF-D1: 'The skill ships brief_criteria.py beside its SKILL.md.' BRF-D2: the shared fixture 'lives in the skill's evals/'. BRF-D8 names evals/score_briefs.py. The ordered slices name the helper and test files.
obligations.statement: Deliver the helper, scorer, fixtures and tests at the specified repository locations.

parts.statement: Spec assignments emit exactly their IDs and full entry text.
Criteria-file assignments emit exactly the file's entries.
Item assignments emit exactly the rendered criteria.

obligations.source: BRF-D1: the first section 'holds the assigned criteria as - **ID** text entries'. BRF-D2 defines spec, criteria-file and item sources.
obligations.statement: Emit exactly the assigned criteria, preserving their full source text.

parts.statement: Entry recognition, section boundaries, continuation joining and fence exclusion determine the source entries.

obligations.source: BRF-D2: 'Spec and file entries follow spec-lint's entry grammar, joined text included', followed by the five rules.
obligations.statement: Read spec and file entries using the five specified grammar rules.

parts.statement: Preservation holds for dispatches generally, including untested assignments and executions outside the evaluation's passing samples.

obligations.source: Scope: 'A dispatch brief must carry exactly the criteria assigned to the work.' BRF-D3 requires exactly the assigned IDs and source text after whitespace collapse.
obligations.statement: Every dispatched brief carries exactly the assigned criteria with their source words preserved.

parts.statement: The complete, separate evidence mapping is preserved in dispatches generally.

obligations.source: Scope: 'It must map each criterion to its planned check, apart from the criterion's text.' BRF-D3 requires evidence IDs and entries to match the plan.
obligations.statement: Every dispatched brief maps each criterion to its planned check separately from its criterion text.

parts.statement: Every helper refusal is relayed and prevents dispatch.
Every absent, blank or infeasible planned check is reported unready and prevents dispatch.

obligations.source: Scope: 'It must refuse when it cannot' and 'A criterion without a feasible planned check is reported unready.' BRF-D4 requires relaying refusal and dispatching nothing. BRF-D5 prohibits dispatch with an unready criterion.
obligations.statement: The writer reports refusals and unready criteria instead of dispatching.

parts.statement: Both modes refuse zero or multiple source flags and name the flags supplied.

obligations.source: BRF-D2: 'Exactly one source flag is given. More than one, or none, refuses as source-conflict.'
obligations.statement: Exactly one source flag is required.

parts.statement: Empty assignments refuse as no-criteria.
Absent spec IDs refuse as unretrievable and name the IDs.
Unreadable sources and briefs refuse as unreadable-source with their required details.
Repeated assigned or defined IDs refuse as duplicate-id.
Non-entry criteria-file content refuses as malformed-criteria, without an additional no-criteria fault.
Invalid checks shapes refuse as malformed-checks.
Failed item rendering refuses as render-failed with the item and cause.
Source-conflict and shared-source failures use the same refusal interface in both modes.

obligations.source: BRF-D4 defines the refusal interface and its eight codes. BRF-D1 gives check its source-comparison role.
obligations.statement: Input failures produce the specified refusal codes, identifying details, empty stdout, one stderr JSON object and exit 2.

parts.statement: Detected faults are aggregated rather than stopping after the first.

obligations.source: BRF-D4: 'One refusal names every fault the helper detects in the sources it can read. Two absent IDs therefore yield one refusal naming both.'
obligations.statement: One refusal aggregates every detected fault in readable sources.

parts.statement: Both sections are present, with no third section, including exit-1 output.
Checks availability never changes the criteria section.

obligations.source: BRF-D1: 'emit mode prints exactly two Markdown sections.' BRF-D5 preserves both sections when criteria are unready.
obligations.statement: Non-refusal emit output consists of exactly the criteria and evidence Markdown sections.

parts.statement: Criteria preservation yields exit 0; missing, added or altered criteria yield exit 1 naming the IDs.
With checks supplied, both sections must be preserved and evidence differences are named.

obligations.source: BRF-D1: check compares a brief with the source and supplied plan. BRF-D3 defines ID-set equality, whitespace normalization, order independence and evidence equality.
obligations.statement: Check accepts precisely preserved criteria and, when supplied a plan, preserved evidence.

parts.statement: Complete plans produce exact assigned-ID evidence and exit 0; well-formed unassigned entries have no effect.
Missing or blank fields produce the specified unready reasons, stderr IDs and exit 1, including absent --checks.
Shape validation covers assigned and unassigned entries, distinguishes absent keys from malformed values, and ignores other keys.

obligations.source: BRF-D5 defines observe/pass strings, missing and blank fields, ignored keys, unassigned entries, readiness reasons and exit statuses.
obligations.statement: The helper implements the planned-check shape, readiness rules and evidence rendering.

parts.statement: The two runtimes produce equivalent results without importable third-party packages.
The helper's implementation uses only standard-library packages.

obligations.source: BRF-D1: 'The helper uses the standard library only, so it runs under uv run or python3 on every supported tool.'
obligations.statement: The helper uses only the standard library and operates under python3 and uv run.

parts.statement: All four instructions appear in the delivered skill text.

obligations.source: BRF-D6 specifies the rewritten acceptance-criteria part and skeleton and those four instructions.
obligations.statement: The skill and skeleton instruct the writer to emit, paste unchanged, check before dispatch, and report refusal or unreadiness.

parts.statement: The writer obtains both sections from emit, pastes them unchanged and executes check before dispatch.

obligations.source: BRF-D6: 'Criteria and evidence come from emit, pasted unchanged, and check runs before dispatch.' BRF-D1 also directs the writer to paste both sections unchanged.
obligations.statement: The writer actually follows the helper route before dispatch.

parts.statement: The fixture, parser markings, both suite readings, missing-fixture failures and specified rule-breaking variants are present.
Every test file and evals directory is pruned so the suites do not ship in deployed trees.

obligations.source: BRF-D2 requires a case for every rule, counterpart markings, both suites reading the fixture, failure when it is absent, and installer pruning of every test file alongside evals.
obligations.statement: The shared fixture exposes grammar drift, and test artifacts are excluded from deployment.

parts.statement: The skill remains within the applicable token caps.

obligations.source: BRF-D6: 'Content-lint's token caps apply.'
obligations.statement: The rewritten skill satisfies the applicable content-lint token caps.

parts.statement: Only acceptance render is called and its rendered criteria are used.
Failed rendering and empty rendering produce their specified refusals.

obligations.source: BRF-D7: --item runs work acceptance render, never resolves the acceptance field itself, and refuses when rendering is unavailable or fails.
obligations.statement: Item criteria come only from the facade renderer, with its specified failure behavior.

parts.statement: F1 and F2 preservation sides pass at the declared threshold.
F1 and F2 evidence sides pass at the declared threshold.
F3 passes with the prescribed refusal report.
F4 and F5 pass with the prescribed refusal reports and details.
F6 and F7 pass with reports identifying their unready criteria.

obligations.source: BRF-D8's fixture table, five-run protocol and threshold rules. S3.5 delivers 'the committed attempts that lock every fixture'.
obligations.statement: The seven fixed generated-brief fixtures obtain current locks under the declared evaluation protocol.

parts.statement: The record contains the required model ID, fingerprint and attestations.
The actual executions use the required model, tool, skill revision, fixed tasks, fresh contexts and tool restrictions.

obligations.source: BRF-D8 requires Claude Opus through the native Agent tool, the source-tree skill by full path, fixed tasks, fresh contexts, no subagent tool, recorded resolved model ID and operator attestations.
obligations.statement: Evaluation execution and its record follow the specified writer protocol.

parts.statement: The stated seeded three-failure cases fail and identify their fixtures.
A conforming output set locks every fixture.
One three-of-five side with all other sides passing awaits its full retest, then passes only with five additional passes.
Remaining initial score counts and combinations of independently retesting sides follow the declared rules.

obligations.source: BRF-D8 defines brief/report forms, rejects missing Form lines, scores F1 and F2 halves separately, passes four of five, retests three of five once, fails lower scores and requires every side to pass.
obligations.statement: The scorer evaluates forms and fixture sides using the complete threshold and retest rules.

parts.statement: Missing scored outputs, named files or required record metadata make the fixture incomplete rather than locked or failed.
An unfinished earned retest is awaiting, rather than incomplete, locked or failed.
More than five named initial or retest outputs cause refusal.

obligations.source: BRF-D8 leaves no-output runs pending, prevents their fixtures from locking, requires full retests and refuses records naming more than five outputs.
obligations.statement: Incomplete evidence stays pending, earned retests await completion, and over-limit named outputs are refused.

parts.statement: Mismatched fingerprints are excluded; matching fingerprints with passing stored runs remain current regardless of changes outside the fingerprint.
A matching fingerprint does not preserve a lock whose stored runs fail after rescoring.
Only fingerprint-affected fixtures rerun, and scorer-only changes dispatch no writer.

obligations.source: BRF-D8 defines the fingerprint, voids only affected locks, reruns only affected fixtures, and requires scorer-only changes to rescore stored outputs without dispatching a writer.
obligations.statement: Fingerprint changes and scorer changes maintain the evaluation of record correctly without unnecessary writer runs.

parts.statement: The scorer refuses later committed attempts with an already-seen fingerprint.
Only the record's named outputs count; unnamed outputs do not affect scoring.
A no-output run is repeated at most twice.
Committed attempts retain their runs, incomplete attempts are completed in place, and unchanged fingerprints are not rerolled by replacing attempt contents.

obligations.source: BRF-D8 permits one attempt per fingerprint, one earned retest, at most two repeats of a no-output run, completion of incomplete attempts in place, and no replacement or reroll.
obligations.statement: Each fingerprint receives only its permitted attempt, retest and missing-output repeats.

parts.statement: Passing, failed, late and unnamed outputs, the record, report and retest evidence remain committed in the specified attempt structure.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: unnamed late outputs 'stay committed'; an attempt is committed under evals/runs/<run-id>/ with outputs, record and report 'whatever it shows', with retests beside it.
obligations.statement: All evaluation evidence is committed and retained, whatever its result.

parts.statement: A demonstrated defect is corrected through a skill change, lock invalidation and reevaluation.

obligations.source: BRF-D8: 'a defect it shows is answered by changing the skill, which voids the lock and runs the fixture again.'
obligations.statement: A defect shown by a failed run behind a lock is answered by changing the skill and reevaluating the affected fixture.

parts.statement: Generated-brief verification has the required current fixture locks.
S3.5 carries verification ownership and parent completion is credited only to the evaluation of record.

obligations.source: BRF-D9: 'S3.5 is the verification child for ACQ-A12 and ACQ-A13' and 'Only the evaluation of record establishes the parents at the generated brief.'
obligations.statement: S3.5 owns parent verification, and only the generated-brief evaluation establishes the parent obligations.

parts.statement: The gates execute the named suites, demonstrated by seeded suite failures turning their gates red.
S3.1's content-tests and ci gates exit 0.
S3.2's content-tests gate exits 0.
S3.3's content-tests gate exits 0.
S3.4's content-lint gate exits 0.

obligations.source: The non-entry testing prose names content-tests and ci as suite gates. The Continuations require content-tests and ci to exit 0 for S3.1, content-tests for S3.2 and S3.3, and content-lint for S3.4.
obligations.statement: The named verification gates execute their suites and produce the required successful gate results.

parts.statement: Unchanged helper runs produce identical results, write no files and share no state across concurrent sources.

obligations.source: The non-entry What-if prose states: 'emit and check read and never write, so running either twice or with nothing changed prints the same result and concurrent runs share nothing'.
obligations.statement: Emit and check are repeatable, read-only and independent across concurrent runs.

ground.reason: BRF-D2 requires both tested agreement on the entry grammar and markings identifying the counterpart parsers. BRF-A9 combines these obligations. Its fixture and mutation checks establish grammar coverage; counterpart markings can be delivered or rejected independently of that coverage.

objections.objection: BRF-A9 makes parser markings and mechanically demonstrated grammar coverage share one acceptance decision.

scenario.expect: The checks pass, while no independent acceptance decision exists for the counterpart markings versus grammar coverage.
scenario.given: Both parsers carry counterpart markings, both suites read the fixture, rule-breaking variants fail cases, and an absent fixture fails both suites.
scenario.when: BRF-A9's checks run and the criterion is accepted.

ground.reason: BRF-D5 promises that planned-check readiness does not change the criteria section. BRF-D1 separately requires exactly two emitted sections. BRF-A22 combines checks for criteria-section stability with the prohibition on a third section. Either result can be delivered without the other.

objections.objection: BRF-A22 bundles preservation across checks configurations with the output's section-count contract.

scenario.expect: The checks pass, while criteria preservation and the section-count contract receive no separate acceptance decisions.
scenario.given: The helper emits identical full criteria sections with absent, complete and incomplete checks, and every emitted output has exactly two sections.
scenario.when: The helper suite evaluates BRF-A22.

ground.reason: The What-if questions promise repeatable results, no file writes, and isolation between concurrent runs. BRF-A30 combines all three. Comparing stdout, stderr and exit status across repeated runs establishes determinism; it does not establish either of the independently deliverable side-effect and isolation obligations.

objections.objection: BRF-A30 makes deterministic output, absence of file writes, and concurrency isolation share one acceptance decision.

scenario.expect: The checks pass, while determinism, absence of writes and concurrency isolation cannot be accepted or rejected independently under this criterion.
scenario.given: The helper and scorer produce identical results on repeated inputs, the helper writes no files, and concurrent helper runs share nothing.
scenario.when: The helper suite evaluates BRF-A30.

ground.reason: The checks exercise the helper and generated outputs, but none checks the promised locations of the shipped artifacts.

objections.objection: The helper can work during evaluation without shipping beside the skill.

scenario.expect: All checks pass, but the delivered skill directory lacks brief_criteria.py.
scenario.given: A working helper outside the skill directory and a writer configured to invoke that copy.
scenario.when: The suites and generated-brief evaluation run.

ground.reason: BRF-A16 establishes preservation at the fixed fixtures' declared threshold. It does not establish the scope's guarantee for every dispatch.

objections.objection: A writer can dispatch criteria that differ from the assignment while every criterion passes.

scenario.expect: The evaluation locks its fixtures, but the dispatched brief omits an assigned criterion.
scenario.given: Passing F1 and F2 records and a writer that preserves their assignments but drops a criterion from an item-sourced assignment.
scenario.when: The writer briefs that item-sourced task.

ground.reason: BRF-A17 observes evidence preservation for F1 and F2 at the declared threshold. The helper checks do not establish what the writer dispatches elsewhere.

objections.objection: A dispatched brief can lack the separate, complete evidence mapping promised by the scope.

scenario.expect: All checks pass, but the dispatched brief has no evidence entry for an assigned criterion.
scenario.given: A conforming helper and passing evaluation records, with a writer that omits evidence on assignments outside F1 and F2.
scenario.when: The writer dispatches another assignment.

ground.reason: BRF-A28 checks instruction text. BRF-A18 and BRF-A19 sample only the no-criteria, absent-ID and unreadable-spec refusals.

objections.objection: The writer can dispatch after a refusal whose case the evaluation does not represent.

scenario.expect: Every check passes, but the writer returns a brief after the helper refuses duplicate-id.
scenario.given: A helper that refuses duplicate IDs correctly and a writer that handles F3 through F5 correctly but ignores duplicate-id refusals.
scenario.when: The assignment contains a duplicate ID.

ground.reason: F6 represents one infeasible pass rule, and F7 represents particular missing-check cases. Their locks do not establish the broader feasibility and non-dispatch obligations.

objections.objection: An infeasible planned check can be dispatched without being reported unready.

scenario.expect: The fixtures lock, but the writer dispatches the criterion without reporting it unready.
scenario.given: A writer that recognizes F6's 'reads well' rule but accepts a check requiring access to an unavailable private service.
scenario.when: The writer receives the inaccessible-service check.

ground.reason: BRF-A24 observes runtime equivalence without third-party packages. That permits optional third-party imports and does not establish the explicit standard-library-only constraint.

objections.objection: The helper can use a third-party package when available while passing the runtime comparison.

scenario.expect: Both runtimes produce identical results and every check passes, despite the non-standard-library import.
scenario.given: A helper that optionally imports a third-party package and falls back to identical standard-library behavior when it is absent.
scenario.when: BRF-A24 compares the isolated python3 run with uv run.

ground.reason: BRF-A28 establishes that instructions are present. Output checks establish acceptable output, rather than whether the writer executed emit and check.

objections.objection: The writer can bypass the helper route required before dispatch.

scenario.expect: All output checks pass, but the writer never invokes emit or runs check before dispatch.
scenario.given: A skill containing all four required instructions and a writer that manually produces correct fixture outputs.
scenario.when: The generated-brief evaluation runs.

ground.reason: BRF-A9 checks repository fixtures and parser suites. No criterion observes the installed tree's exclusion of test files.

objections.objection: Test files can ship despite the commitment that neither suite exists in a deployed tree.

scenario.expect: All repository checks pass, but the deployed skill contains its test files without their pruned evals fixture.
scenario.given: Passing suites and an installer that prunes evals directories but copies adjacent test files.
scenario.when: The skill is installed.

ground.reason: The continuation requires content-lint to exit 0. That observation establishes the gate result, rather than independently establishing that the skill satisfies the applicable token caps.

objections.objection: An over-cap skill can be accepted if the gate does not apply its cap to that skill.

scenario.expect: The gate exits 0 and every criterion passes, but the rewritten skill exceeds its applicable token cap.
scenario.given: A skill containing the required instructions and passing fixture outputs, with content-lint omitting that skill from its cap check.
scenario.when: The S3.4 checks run.

ground.reason: BRF-A26 observes model metadata and operator attestations. Those artifact properties do not establish the actual execution protocol.

objections.objection: The evaluation can lock outputs produced without the required writer, source skill, fresh contexts or tool restrictions.

scenario.expect: All records and outputs pass, although the required execution protocol was not followed.
scenario.given: Conforming outputs produced in reused contexts from a deployed skill, with records naming Claude Opus and attesting the required protocol.
scenario.when: The scorer reads the committed records.

ground.reason: BRF-A27 covers conforming sets and three-failure sets. BRF-A32 covers one three-of-five side while every other side passes. Other threshold cases and combinations have no complete check.

objections.objection: The scorer can mishandle four-of-five results or independent retests while passing every specified check.

scenario.expect: Every specified check passes, but the scorer refuses to lock the four-of-five side.
scenario.given: A scorer that handles all-five passes, three failures, and BRF-A32's single-side retest correctly, but treats an initial four-of-five result as awaiting a retest.
scenario.when: A fixture receives four passing runs and one failed run.

ground.reason: BRF-A33 checks fingerprint mismatch and matching fingerprints whose runs still pass. It does not check the matching-fingerprint case whose stored runs fail after rescoring.

objections.objection: A scorer change can leave a failed stored lock marked current.

scenario.expect: The listed checks pass on their specified cases, but the failed stored lock remains current.
scenario.given: A scorer that invalidates mismatched fingerprints but retains a matching lock's current flag when rescoring makes its runs fail.
scenario.when: It rescores that matching-fingerprint lock after a scorer change.

ground.reason: Fingerprint checks observe lock currency. No criterion observes which writer runs the operator dispatches following a change.

objections.objection: The operator can rerun unaffected fixtures or dispatch writers after a scorer-only change.

scenario.expect: Every stored-result check passes, but unnecessary writer runs occur.
scenario.given: Current passing locks and an operator that dispatches writers whenever any evaluation file changes.
scenario.when: Only score_briefs.py changes.

ground.reason: The document assigns the repeat limit to the operator. Neither output-count checks nor record checks observe the actual number of no-output retries.

objections.objection: A pending run can be retried more than twice without failing a criterion.

scenario.expect: The record names five passing outputs and all checks pass, although the repeat limit was exceeded.
scenario.given: A run that produces no output on its first three executions.
scenario.when: The operator repeats it a third time and records the resulting output.

ground.reason: BRF-A34 detects two committed attempts with the same fingerprint. It does not establish that a committed attempt was completed in place or that its failed runs were retained.

objections.objection: An operator can reroll an unchanged fingerprint by replacing outputs within the existing attempt.

scenario.expect: Only one attempt remains visible and all checks pass, despite the forbidden reroll.
scenario.given: A committed failed attempt and an operator who replaces its failed outputs and record with passing reruns under the same fingerprint.
scenario.when: The scorer checks the amended directory.

ground.reason: BRF-A26 checks named outputs and metadata. BRF-A35 ignores unnamed outputs. Neither establishes commitment and retention of every output, report and retest artifact.

objections.objection: Failed, late or unnamed outputs can be discarded, and the required attempt report can remain uncommitted.

scenario.expect: The scorer locks the fixture and every check passes, but the discarded output and attempt report are absent from committed evidence.
scenario.given: Five named passing outputs, an additional late output, and a locally generated report.
scenario.when: The operator commits only the named outputs and record.

ground.reason: The lock criteria permit a failed run at four of five. No criterion checks that a defect shown by that run causes a skill change and invalidation of the lock.

objections.objection: A fixture can remain locked while a committed failed run demonstrates an unanswered skill defect.

scenario.expect: The fixture locks and every criterion passes, but the demonstrated defect remains and the skill fingerprint is unchanged.
scenario.given: Four correct F3 reports and one F3 brief that demonstrates the writer dispatching after no-criteria.
scenario.when: The operator accepts the four-of-five lock without changing the skill.

ground.reason: The criteria establish helper, scorer, skill-text and evaluation results. None checks the verification child's ownership or the rule governing parent completion.

objections.objection: The parent obligations can be credited to implementation evidence without the required verification-child ownership.

scenario.expect: Every criterion eventually passes, but parent verification was credited to helper suites and S3.5 was not recorded as its verification child.
scenario.given: Passing helper suites and a tracker workflow that closes the parent obligations from implementation children.
scenario.when: The implementation children close, before the evaluation of record is established.

ground.reason: BRF-D8 defines the report form as a message that 'relays what the helper printed on stderr', but for F6 the helper exits 0 with nothing on stderr (the criterion has a planned, nonblank check; unready is the writer's judgment per BRF-D5), so the definition and BRF-A20's pass condition admit two readings with opposite verdicts.

objections.objection: The criteria leave open whether an F6 report may name an unready ID the helper never reported: under a strict reading of the report-form definition no output can pass F6 (the helper printed nothing to relay), while under the intended reading a writer-authored report naming the ID passes — the same output is scored both ways depending on which reading the scorer takes.
objections.obligation: BRF-D8 report-form definition; BRF-D5 feasibility judgment

scenario.expect: One reading fails the run because the report relays helper stderr that does not exist and so is not 'the report form'; the other passes it because naming the unready ID is exactly what F6 asks — conflicting verdicts on identical output.
scenario.given: The F6 fixture: three criteria, each with a planned check whose fields are nonblank strings, one pass rule reading 'a reviewer confirms it reads well'; the helper exits 0 and prints nothing on stderr.
scenario.when: The writer judges that check infeasible and returns a report naming that ID as unready, and the scorer judges the run against BRF-A20 and the BRF-D8 report definition.

ground.reason: BRF-A35 (and BRF-D8) say the scorer 'refuses the attempt' when a record names six runs, but no criterion assigns a status to the fixture behind a refused attempt: BRF-A26's incomplete conditions do not cover an over-long record, and locked/failed are plainly inapplicable, so the outcome the refusal produces is undecided.

objections.objection: The criteria leave open what the scorer reports for a fixture whose attempt it refuses: one reading reports the fixture incomplete (the attempt is not complete), another drops it from the evaluation of record the way BRF-A33 drops a not-current lock, and a third treats the attempt as failed — three divergent outcomes from the same committed state.

scenario.expect: Depending on the reading, the fixture is reported incomplete, reported absent from the record entirely, or reported failed — diverging outcomes the criteria do not decide between.
scenario.given: A committed attempt whose record names six outputs for a fixture's five runs, with all five named outputs passing.

ground.reason: BRF-D2 states a criteria file follows all grammar rules but the second, which gives headings a defined role (rule 4: a heading ends the entry), yet BRF-A7 refuses as malformed-criteria on any 'nonblank line outside an entry', and a heading outside an entry is exactly that — the two readings disagree on whether a heading may appear in a criteria file at all.

objections.objection: The criteria leave open whether a heading line is legal in a criteria file: under BRF-A7's blanket wording every heading outside an entry is malformed and rule 4's heading clause is dead for criteria files, while under the grammar's own applicability (rules 1, 3, 4, 5 apply) headings are structural entry-enders and the file parses — the same file is refused or accepted depending on the reading.

scenario.expect: Under BRF-A7's wording the heading is a nonblank line outside an entry and emit refuses as malformed-criteria; under the grammar's treatment of headings as entry-enders the entries parse and emit prints them — incompatible outcomes for one input.
scenario.given: A criteria file that opens with a heading line such as '# Review criteria' followed by well-formed '- **ID** text' entries.
scenario.when: `emit --criteria FILE` parses the file and the result is judged against BRF-A7 and the BRF-D2 grammar.

ground.reason: BRF-D5 and BRF-A12 define malformed-checks only for non-JSON, non-object top level, non-object entries, and non-string observe/pass values. A JSON object with the same ID as a duplicate key is valid JSON and breaks none of those rules, so no refusal applies; the parser silently keeps one of the two entries (Python's json keeps the last), and which one wins is pinned by no criterion. The same criterion can therefore be judged ready or unready depending on key order in the file, and no test detects it.

objections.objection: The criteria let a checks file carrying one ID twice — one entry complete, one with a blank pass rule — through with an outcome that depends on key order rather than on any rule the document states, so a criterion's readiness is decided by an accident of the input.

scenario.expect: The document implies emit decides readiness from one of the two entries, but no criterion says which, or that the file refuses as malformed-checks or duplicate-id
scenario.given: A checks file that is well-formed under BRF-D5 except that one assigned ID appears as a key twice, the first entry with a blank pass rule and the second with a complete observation and pass rule
scenario.when: emit runs with --checks over that file

ground.reason: BRF-D2 names three source flags (--spec with --ids, --criteria, --item) and requires exactly one source flag, and BRF-A29 tests only 'more than one source flag or none'. Whether --ids counts as a source flag when paired with --item or --criteria is never stated: '--spec PATH --ids ID,...' binds --ids to --spec, but no decision or criterion covers '--item ID --ids X' or '--criteria FILE --ids X'. The helper could refuse as source-conflict, ignore --ids, or filter the item's criteria, and each reading is compatible with every criterion as written.

objections.objection: The criteria let a dispatch that pairs --ids with --item or --criteria produce an unspecified result — possibly a brief carrying the item's full criteria where the writer asked for a subset, or the reverse — with no criterion checking which.

scenario.expect: The document implies either a source-conflict refusal or a defined filtering of the rendered criteria, but no criterion tests either outcome
scenario.given: A work item whose rendering holds several criteria, and a writer invoking emit with --item together with --ids naming a subset
scenario.when: emit runs with both flags
